pinned_repository.name: math
pinned_repository.date_interpretation: Commit date, not inferred public-release timestamp.

review_scope.mode: Mechanism-level reading and statement/literature comparison by an AI agent; not an external human referee report or a theorem-proof acceptance.
review_scope.mathematical_claim_status: Released manuscripts are treated as proposed proofs. Established prior theorems and preceding 2026 preprint claims are labeled separately.

reads.symmetric_mahler: Critical lens, holomorphic-mass, feasibility, simplex, zero-deficit, and median proofs read, together with introduction and selected convex preliminaries.
reads.general_mahler: Introduction, cone reduction, full simultaneous normalization, entropy-to-cone-product assembly, linear-field bound assembly/rigidity, finite scalar certificate section and strict-segment statement inspected. Quadratic/layer/long segment appendices were not exhaustively independently checked.
reads.direct_crouzeix: Main theorem, positive kernel and coefficient estimate, resolvent expansion, complete analytic-domain bound and approximation passages read.
reads.structural_crouzeix: Main structural/representation statements and ordered density-comparison proof inspected; the entire supporting density-separation/local-projection construction was not independently checked.

executions.standalone_jordan_control: Parent's exact checker reported separately; the algebraic control in this fragment was independently derived directly.

limits: No claim that downloaded paper proofs were compiled or formally checked.
Comparator challenge templates contain intentional placeholder sorry proofs and declare targets; their placeholders are not evidence about the released solution proof's completeness.
A mechanism map and absence of a demonstrated defect do not certify these proposed solutions.

families.statement: For all n>=1, origin-symmetric compact convex K with nonempty interior: |K||K polar|>=4^n/n!; equality iff an invertible linear image of a Hanner body.
families.proposed_step: Sharp complex boundary-feasibility probability bound transferred through a disjoint polar-simplex identity; equality converted into metric medians through zero-deficit product-neighborhood and compactness arguments.
decisive_checks: Exact mass/flux normalization and high-power boundary limit
Disjointness and Jacobian constant in the feasible-simplex identity
Integral zero deficit yielding a universal feasibility witness despite degenerating row bases
Endpoint lens asymptotic yielding the median property
families.novelty_assessment: Unusual synthesis with claimed all-dimensional sharp scope; no first-ever lens, complex volume-product method or norm classification claim.

families.statement: For all n>=1, compact convex full-dimensional K: inf over interior z of |K||(K-z) polar| >= (n+1)^(n+1)/(n!)^2; equality iff K is a simplex.
reused_ingredients: Gaussian covariance representations and inverse Ornstein--Uhlenbeck operators
families.proposed_step: Simultaneous coordinate/covariance normalization with a noncommuting matrix quadratic; tuned auxiliary scalar curve absorbs the full spectral/layer error through a global strict segment inequality; zero errors force orthant geometry.
decisive_checks: Existence and invariance bounds for coupled normalization without assuming matrices commute
Whole-real-line strict segment absorption, including divided differences, interpolation and tails
Transfer from finite rational node witnesses to global scalar estimates
From zero commutator/layer errors to coordinatewise projection and orthant cone
families.finite_arithmetic: Supplied runner has ten programs, requires Python 3 and SymPy 1.14.0 with assertions enabled; JSON failure fields must be inspected separately from process exit status. Not run in this review.
families.novelty_assessment: Proposed all-dimensional mechanism beyond prior local simplex minimality and preceding general three-dimensional preprint; no first cone reduction or Gaussian covariance formula claim.

families.statement: For arbitrary positive integers n,m, A in M_n(C), every degree d>=0 and arbitrary B_k in M_m(C), norm(sum A^k tensor B_k)<=2 max over W(A) norm(sum z^k B_k). Points and segments included; universal sharpness already occurs at scalar coefficients.
reused_ingredients: Convex double-layer positivity and mass normalization
families.proposed_step: Fourier contraction gives weighted coefficient estimates compatible with separate FG and GF tests, supplying diagonal upper bounds and a cross lower bound uniform in independent coefficient size.
decisive_checks: Unit-mass positive kernel and positive-to-negative Fourier contraction
Constant-term weight and both multiplication orders in the complete extremal argument
Matching diagonal/cross estimates before the elementary final block inequality
Analytic convex outer approximation for numerical ranges with empty interior
preceding_preprint_claims: Lorist--Schwenninger scalar constant 2, v2 17 August 2026; their Section 3(iv) highlights the amplification obstruction.
Åhag--Czyż--Virtanen complete constant 2 for base order <=3, v4 21 September 2026.
families.novelty_assessment: Claimed advance is arbitrary-dimensional complete constant 2; neither a first scalar constant-two claim nor a first positive boundary representation.

families.statement: For finite matrices in bounded convex domains with regular real-analytic Jordan boundary, an attained optimal similarity has condition number <=2 and a single continuous positive density of mass identity represents all matrix-valued analytic tests. Companion also claims complete bounds for bounded operators on arbitrary complex Hilbert spaces and functions holomorphic near the closed numerical range.
reused_ingredients: Positive boundary representation and similarity methods
families.proposed_step: Attained optimal metric linked to an ordered-density comparison yielding condition number <=2 and one representation common to independent coefficient sizes.
decisive_checks: Extremal/supporting-density construction and local projection bridge
Ordered left/right module estimates in comparison lemma
Correct regular-domain hypotheses for the structural result
Finite-compression and functional-calculus passage to arbitrary Hilbert spaces
families.novelty_assessment: Stronger structural formulation of the claimed complete sharp bound; only selected decisive passages independently inspected.

primary_priors.verified_identity: Renan Gross; A conformal Skorokhod embedding; Electronic Communications in Probability 24 (2019); DOI 10.1214/19-ECP272; 11 pp. Article number omitted because original publisher access failed in this audit.
primary_priors.supports: Explicit conformal boundary construction for a uniform coordinate; released lens is its rotation. It does not itself prove the Mahler volume estimate.

primary_priors.verified_identity: Jean-Pierre Demailly; Monge--Ampère operators, Lelong numbers and intersection theory; Complex Analysis and Geometry (1993), pp. 115--193; DOI 10.1007/978-1-4757-9771-8_4.
primary_priors.content_location: Sections 3 and 5: Monge--Ampère operators, generalized Lelong-number framework
primary_priors.supports: Classical complex mass/flux framework behind the released isolated-zero estimate. The exact feasibility normalization remains a released-paper claim.

documentation_findings.status: Confirmed documentation inconsistency; not a demonstrated mathematical or solution-proof defect.
documentation_findings.details: The document says the nonsymmetric conjecture is not included, then asserts the general bound and simplex equality; it links GeneralMahler.lean, which declares precisely that target.
documentation_findings.interpretation: General theorem statement correspondence is present. Formal proof success must be established by checking actual solution artifacts, not these placeholder challenge templates.

independent_controls.derivation: For a unit x in C^2, x*Ax=2 conjugate(x1) x2. Magnitudes fill [0,1] and phases are arbitrary, so W(A) is the closed unit disk. A*A=diag(0,4), hence norm(A)=2 and max_W |p|=1.
independent_controls.conclusion: Every universal scalar or complete constant is at least 2. This sharpness control does not verify the claimed upper bound.
